Title: Document 3
Subtitle: Bernhard Baumann, Jesuit official in Heidelberg, report to Elector Maximilian of Bavaria on efforts to re-Catholicize previously Protestant areas after the Catholic victory in that region, 1628
Content: `text(Four hundred)` in the town and `1text(,)200` outside it have been freed from heresy; on feast days we get around `700` communicants in the Church of the Holy Spirit. We alone look after parish duties, visit the sick and converts daily, conduct catechism inside the town and outside, and deliver `text(two)` sermons on `text(Sundays)`. These crowds are gathered with great difficulty; since only `text(six months)` ago the richer townspeople were so obstinate, that `text(two or three hundred)` declared they would emigrate if they were forced to convert. Then entire districts (they had arranged this in advance) declared they would keep the faith of their ancestors, because we could not steal this like other possessions. Since the orders arrived from Munich [to intensify Catholic conversions] they have used unbelievable deceptions to try to circumvent these. Furthermore, they complain to the Holy Roman Emperor, but the secular government, to its undying credit, knew how to stop this.
